Alice — thanks for the profile. Put together a concise onramp proposal below so procurement has concrete acceptance gates to include in the SOW/DocuSign.

Proposed recommendation (summary):
- GPU fleet: mix of 8xA100-80GB + 4xH100-80GB for headroom. H100s used for top-end burst and heavy-context evaluation.
- Measured targets to commit against: sustained 1,000 QPS (short requests), peak 1,800 QPS bursts (weekend), 99th pct latency <= 350ms p99 on 1k token context.
- Validation window: 72-hour staged validation (see phases below) during the commitment week.
- Canary cutover: 6-hour progressive shift by traffic weight (10%/25%/50%/100%) with live health checks and automated rollback on specified SLO failures.

Validation phases (detailed):
1) Smoke + correctness (Day 0): run 10k requests from your provided prompt set to validate output parity with hosted baseline.
2) Load ramp (Day 1): step ramp to 60% of committed throughput over 6 hours, monitor token throughput, KV-cache hit rate, and memory growth.
3) Sustained soak (Day 2): 24-hour sustained at target sustained throughput (1k QPS) including stochastic short bursts to simulate weekend profile.
4) Burst & failover exercise (Day 3): execute three controlled peak bursts up to 1.8k QPS and validate fallback to smaller model variants with <2% error-rate increase.

Acceptance criteria (SOWable):
- Throughput: sustained 95% of target QPS for 24h during soak window.
- Correctness: automated prompt-set pass-rate >= 98% (exact evaluation metrics to be embedded).
- Latency: 99th percentile token latency <= 350ms during soak.
- Stability: zero OOM events, <0.5% error responses, KV-cache cold-start recovery within 90s.

Operational handoffs and dependencies:
- Redwood will provide a dedicated staging cluster and an isolated canary pool for the validation window.
- Helios must supply the canonical prompt set for correctness checks and a support rotation for the canary window.
- Procurement: Ben to confirm invoice schedule and start-of-commit date once validation windows are locked.

Proposed timeline (you said target Jan 4 start):
- Week of Dec 13: procurement paperwork and final SOW.
- Dec 27-Jan 2: reserved capacity provisioning and dry-run (internal).
- Jan 3-6: customer validation window (72-hour as described).
- Jan 7: planned cutover to dedicated if acceptance metrics met.

I'll attach a stress matrix / test checklist after Karthik and Ben review. Proposed sync: Thursday 11/14 at 10am PT.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Vanessa — added a couple of technical constraints and a stress-test inventory. Attaching the dedicated stress matrix and the exact k6 scenarios we'll run.

Key technical notes:
- Model shards: LlamaX-v2 will be deployed with tensor-slicing; expect 4-way shard on A100 and 6-way on H100 for the large config.
- Batch sizing: target dynamic batching with max batch 64 for short requests; steady-state scheduling uses continuous-batching to keep GPU utilization >80%.
- KV-cache warmup: expect ~10–12 minutes to reach steady-state hit-rates if you use persistent session pins. We'll require an initial warmup with representative traffic.
- Mirroring: we'll mirror 10% of your live traffic into the staging cluster during the Dec 27-Jan 2 dry-run for smoke validation.

Stress test inventory (high level):
- k6 spike profile: 0 -> 1.8k QPS over 60s, sustain 5m, repeat 3x.
- Long-context soak: 12h run at 600 QPS with 4k token contexts to validate mem behavior.
- Failover sim: disrupt two nodes (simulated) and confirm <5% drop in throughput and <2x latency penalty during graceful degraded mode.

Attachment: dedicated_stress_matrix.pdf (checklist + k6 scripts).

I'll coordinate with infra to schedule the mirror and the stress windows. Should we formally lock the dry-run dates now? Helios jan start is tight; locking provisioning by Dec 20 gives us runway.

-karthik
